# Knowledge Knowledge is Row-Bot's local memory: the facts, people, projects, preferences and relationships it has saved from conversations, documents and your own edits, connected as a graph. Row-Bot recalls relevant memories when they help a conversation. For the relationship between thread history, memory, documents, the graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle, read [How Memory Becomes Knowledge](/docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle). ## Where To Find It - **Home Knowledge** is where you see and manage memories. - **Settings Memory** turns memory on or off, shows graph health, configures the [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault), and holds **Delete all knowledge**. - **Settings Documents** configures document search and its embedding model. ## Views Choose a view at the top of the Knowledge tab: - **Graph** draws memories and their connections and lets the layout settle into place. It opens with up to 2,000 memories; **Show all memories** draws up to 5,000. Use **Zoom in**, **Zoom out** and **Fit**, and hide or show memory types from the legend. - **List** shows the whole library, newest first, with search across every memory. - **Review** is the queue of memories Row-Bot was unsure about. **Mark as reviewed**, **Edit memory** or **Archive memory** settles each one. - **Activity** shows recent recalls (memory used or skipped in a conversation) and recent changes. **Filters** narrow the graph and list by source, status and memory type, show or hide you as the central memory, and can hide unconnected memories. ## A Memory's Details Select a memory to see its description, memory type, status, source, confidence and when it was updated, its connections, where it came from, and its history (created, edited by you, refined by Row-Bot, last recalled). From there: - **Edit memory** corrects it. - **Merge or replace** folds a duplicate into another memory and moves its connections. - **Archive memory** keeps it but stops it being recalled; **Restore memory** brings it back. - **Delete memory** removes it, its connections and its search entries after you confirm. Select several memories to delete them together, up to 100 at a time. Use **Add memory** to save something yourself. ## Dream Cycle Dream Cycle tidies memory overnight: it merges duplicates, enriches thin memories and infers missing links. Turn it on and choose its hours in **Settings Preferences Overnight tidy-up**. **Run Dream Cycle** on the Knowledge tab reviews what it would do and runs it now after you confirm. Its history is in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/). ## Common Workflow 1. Open Home Knowledge after a few useful chats or document imports. 2. Search for the topic you care about, or open **Review**. 3. Open a memory and check its source. 4. Correct, merge, archive or delete misleading memories. 5. Rely on recall once the important memories are right. ## What Is Saved Memories are local Row-Bot data. They are sent to a model provider only as relevant context in a conversation that uses that provider. ## Troubleshooting - If Knowledge is empty, turn on memory in Settings Memory or add documents in Settings Documents. - If a memory is wrong, edit, merge or archive it rather than deleting whole topics. - If recall feels noisy, review the **Review** queue and archive stale memories. Continue with [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault) and [Provenance And Repair](/docs/knowledge/provenance-repair) for the file-output and recovery workflows.

## Wiki Vault

Route: /docs/knowledge/wiki-vault

Keep a local Markdown vault of Row-Bot's memories, with readable file names, and sync your edits back.

# Wiki Vault Wiki Vault writes your memories and their connections as linked Markdown articles in a folder you choose, so you can read them in Obsidian or any editor. It is an output of the local knowledge graph, not a replacement for the underlying memory and provenance records. ## Configure The Vault 1. Open **Settings Memory** and find **Wiki vault**. 2. Turn on **Enable Wiki Vault** and choose the vault folder with **Browse**. Choosing a folder needs the Row-Bot desktop app; pick a folder separate from application code and important personal notes while you test. 3. Save the configuration, then use **Rebuild managed wiki files** to write every article. 4. Open the articles in your editor and check links, titles and source notes. Articles have readable names: a memory called "Garden plan" becomes `Garden plan.md` in the folder for its type. When two memories share a name, or a note of your own already uses it, Row-Bot adds a short code to the new file name instead of overwriting anything. A renamed memory's article is renamed with it. ## What Row-Bot Writes And Leaves Alone Row-Bot keeps a record of the articles it wrote and only ever updates or moves those. Notes you create yourself in the vault are never changed or deleted. Articles from an earlier version are adopted in place with the same names, so existing links keep working. Files Row-Bot replaced are moved aside for your review, not deleted; **Show moved files** lists them. ## Your Edits When you edit an article in the vault, **Sync vault edits** brings the change back to the memory. If the memory changed in Row-Bot too, **Resolve versions** lets you choose between the database version and the vault version. Correct important facts in Knowledge first when you can, so the graph remains the source of truth. ## Privacy The vault is local, but it is deliberately easy to open in other software or sync with a third-party folder. Treat the destination as an export boundary. Review it before placing it in cloud storage, a shared repository, or a publishing system. ## Troubleshooting - If articles are missing, check that memory is on and the vault folder reads **Available**, then rebuild. - If **Browse** opens no folder picker, use the Row-Bot desktop app; a browser can't choose folders on this computer. - If links duplicate, run Knowledge repair before rebuilding the vault. - If private material appears, correct or remove its source memory, rebuild, and review the destination before sharing.

## Knowledge Provenance And Repair

Route: /docs/knowledge/provenance-repair

Trace where knowledge came from, correct records, repair relations, and rebuild derived outputs safely.

# Knowledge Provenance And Repair Knowledge is useful only when you can tell where it came from. Review provenance before relying on a memory, document fact, entity, or relation for consequential work. ## Review A Record 1. Open **Home Knowledge** and search or filter to the topic. 2. Select the memory to open its details. 3. Check its source, timestamps, type, confidence or status, and related entities. 4. Compare important claims with the original conversation or document. 5. Correct, merge, or remove the record if it is misleading. ## Repair Order Use the smallest repair that fixes the problem: 1. Correct a title, type, description, or relation. 2. Merge a duplicate entity when both records refer to the same thing. 3. Remove a bad relation without deleting sound entities. 4. Rebuild derived indexes if search still returns stale results. 5. Rebuild Wiki Vault output only after the graph is correct. Monitor's **History** (Dream Cycle and Extraction) and Knowledge's **Activity** view help explain background changes. A repair should preserve useful source evidence and avoid touching unrelated memories. ## Recovery Before a large repair or migration, back up with **Settings Data Back up and restore**, or close Row-Bot and copy the active data directory. Restore the whole related data set together rather than mixing database files from different moments. If the app offers a built-in repair action, read its scope and completion message before manually replacing files. ## Safety Boundary Deleting a thread does not necessarily mean every derived record disappears immediately, and deleting one graph entity can affect linked output. Review the exact record and its relationships first. Never run repair tests against a personal data directory.

## Computer Use

Route: /docs/computer-use/

Set up and safely use Row-Bot's opt-in native Windows and macOS application control.

# Computer Use Computer Use is Row-Bot's provider-neutral tool for operating native Windows and macOS applications. It is separate from browser automation: use Browser for web pages and Computer Use only when the task must interact with a desktop application window. Computer Use is a beta feature. It is off by default, supports one interactive local task at a time, and is unavailable to schedules, channels, background workflows, child agents, plugins, external MCP callers, mobile clients, and headless or server sessions. ## Set It Up 1. Open **Settings System** and choose **Browser and computer use**. 2. Under **Desktop apps**, open the **Computer Use (Beta)** setup and read the capability and privacy summary. 3. Choose **Install**. Row-Bot shows the required Cua Driver telemetry disclosure before it downloads or starts anything. 4. Choose **Continue** only if you accept the disclosure. Row-Bot downloads the pinned Cua Driver 0.20.0 full archive for your platform, verifies its SHA-256, and extracts it into Row-Bot's private data directory. Upgrading from an older reviewed driver requires accepting the expanded version-2 telemetry notice again. 5. On macOS, grant Accessibility and Screen Recording to the Row-Bot process when prompted, then choose **Recheck**. Restart the same process after changing permissions if the status asks you to. 6. Turn on **Computer Use (Beta)** after the setup card reports ready. Install, Repair, Reinstall, Remove, and system-binary controls affect only the optional driver. Row-Bot never runs the upstream installer or updater. A custom system binary is accepted only after explicit opt-in and version verification. ## Run A Native Task Ask from a normal local desktop chat and name the application and desired outcome. Row-Bot discovers applications and windows, acquires one exclusive task lease, and binds actions to the selected target window. It can launch an allowlisted application, observe that window, click, type, press keys, scroll, and drag when the current policy permits the operation. When accessibility data is insufficient, Row-Bot may send one ephemeral target-window screenshot to the Vision model configured in Settings. The live control card shows sanitized state and a shielded thumbnail; screenshot bytes are not written to chat, durable memory, replay history, logs, or tool results. ## Stop Or Take Over - **Stop** cancels queued work and releases the session. - **Take over** cancels queued mutation and pauses the lease so you can interact directly. - **Resume** requires Row-Bot to observe the target again before it can act. Window replacement, permission loss, target changes, or driver failure invalidates stale state. Row-Bot must reacquire and observe before another mutation. ## Safety Boundaries Computer Use blocks terminals, password managers, Row-Bot itself, secure desktops, elevation prompts, security settings, and attempts to handle credentials, one-time codes, CAPTCHAs, biometrics, or operating-system permission dialogs. Consequential actions use approval policy at the point of risk, and external handoff flows stay with the user. The reviewed Cua 0.20.0 telemetry sends pseudonymous installation/process-session identifiers and bounded product, platform, client, tool/outcome, duration/output, aggregate session/config/cursor/recording, permission, and lifecycle categories to Cua's EU PostHog endpoint. Its tagged event builders do not receive prompts, tool arguments/results, typed text, screenshots, accessibility trees, app/window names, URLs, paths, raw config/cursor values, or raw errors. Row-Bot adds no first-party telemetry and keeps its prompts, files, memories, secrets, screenshots, tool arguments, and channel content outside Cua telemetry. For the exact allowlist and reviewed dependency record, see [Computer Use Beta: architecture and security decision](https://github.com/siddsachar/row-bot/blob/main/docs/COMPUTER_USE_SECURITY.md). ## Troubleshooting - If setup reports an archive or checksum error, choose **Repair** and retry on a trusted network. - If macOS reports missing permission, use the provided buttons to open Accessibility and Screen Recording settings, grant the running Row-Bot process, restart it, and recheck. - If the requested app is blocked, do not work around the policy with a terminal or generic MCP tool. Operate it manually or use a narrower supported application. - If a session is busy, stop or finish the active Computer Use task before starting another. - If the target window closes or changes, ask Row-Bot to reacquire it before resuming.

## Monitor

Route: /docs/monitor/

See Row-Bot's latest health checks, fix problems in one click, and read activity, maintenance, history and logs.

# Monitor Monitor shows whether Row-Bot is healthy, what needs attention and what recently happened. Use it when a workflow, channel, account, model, background job, knowledge extraction or Dream Cycle needs investigation. ## Where To Find It Choose **Home**, then the **Monitor** tab. When something needs attention, the sidebar's attention indicator says so ("1 thing needs attention") and opens Monitor. ## Checks Are Kept Row-Bot keeps the last result of every check, with its time, so the tiles stay current when you switch tabs or restart the app. - **Checks on this computer** (disk space, databases, the scheduler, memory extraction, Dream Cycle, the search index, documents, the wiki vault, channels and the chosen model) run by themselves at start-up and every 15 minutes. They make no network requests. - **Connection checks** contact your model providers, accounts and the internet. They run once an hour while **Check connections every hour** is on, and whenever you choose **Run diagnosis**. Turn the switch off to run them only when you ask. - A check that turns red raises the sidebar's attention indicator and appears in Overview's **Needs you**. ## Needs Attention And Fixes **Needs attention** lists each problem with the one fix that addresses it: | Problem | Fix | | --- | --- | | A channel stopped | **Restart** the channel, the same reviewed start as its own settings in Settings Apps. | | An account sign-in expired | **Reconnect** Google or X. | | Another channel, account or app problem | **Open ... settings** opens its page in Settings Apps. | | No default model | **Choose a model**. | | A setting needs a change | **Open ... settings** at the exact row, such as the public link in Devices & remote access. | | Disk, network or Ollama | **Check ... again**. | Failed workflows offer **Run ... again** on Overview. ## Health Tiles Six tiles summarise the areas Row-Bot depends on: **Model runtime**, **Channels**, **MCP and tools**, **Scheduler**, **Knowledge** and **System**. Each shows its worst check and that check's fix. Open a tile for every check in it, when each was last checked, and each problem's fix. **Run diagnosis** runs every check now. **Copy diagnosis report** copies a plain summary you can paste into a support request. **Start-up warnings** lists anything Row-Bot reported when it started. ## Activity, Maintenance And History - **Activity** charts extraction, Dream Cycle, workflow runs and channel events over **24 hours** or **7 days**. - **Maintenance** shows when knowledge extraction and Dream Cycle last ran and what they did: memories saved, conversations read, contradictions blocked, duplicates merged, memories enriched and links inferred. - **History** lists each Dream Cycle and extraction run with its changes and errors. ## Logs **Logs** shows Row-Bot's local log. Filter by level, **Search logs**, **Follow** new lines, **Collapse repeats**, and **Copy** the visible lines. ## Common Workflow 1. Reproduce or observe the issue. 2. Open Monitor and read **Needs attention**. 3. Use the suggested fix, or open the tile for detail. 4. Choose **Run diagnosis** to confirm, then check **Logs** if the problem remains. 5. Copy only non-sensitive details into a support request. ## What Is Saved Check results, logs and maintenance history are local Row-Bot data. Logs may include file names, conversation names, provider names, channel names or workflow names, so review them before sharing. ## Troubleshooting - If a tile shows **Checking...**, the first checks are still running. - If a connection check is old, choose **Run diagnosis** or turn on **Check connections every hour**. - If Dream Cycle never runs, turn it on in **Settings Preferences Overnight tidy-up**. - If a channel keeps stopping, open its app in **Settings Apps** (such as **Apps Telegram**), choose **Open**, and check its credentials before restarting it.

## Home: Insights

Route: /docs/home/insights

Review what Row-Bot noticed about its skills, settings and memory, and apply or reject its proposals in Home Insights.

# Home: Insights Insights is where Row-Bot reports what it noticed while working: a skill that keeps failing, two skills that overlap, a setting worth changing, a memory that looks wrong, or a problem worth sending as feedback. Nothing changes until you choose; every proposal is a draft for your review. ## Where To Find It Choose **Home**, then the **Insights** tab, or **Open Insights** from Overview's **Learned this week** card. Insights belong to the owner on this computer. ## Reading An Insight Each insight shows its severity (Critical, Error, Warning, Info or Suggestion), what Row-Bot found, when it found it, and a suggested next step. Row-Bot says when an insight may be out of date: it was found while another chat model was in use, or it has not been seen again for two weeks. Use **All** or **Pinned** to filter the feed, **Refresh** to read it again, **Pin** to keep an insight in view, and **Dismiss** to hide it (with **Undo**). ## Proposals - **Suggest a fix** asks Row-Bot to prepare proposals for an insight that has none yet. - **Apply proposal** makes the change, such as creating or updating a skill. Afterwards the insight says exactly what happened. - **Reject proposal** declines it. - Some proposals are review only: merging skills, changing a setting, or correcting a memory. Row-Bot can't make that change itself, so make it yourself if you agree, then reject the proposal. - **Open investigation draft** opens a prepared conversation for a deeper look. - **Copy feedback** copies a feedback report you can send yourself; Row-Bot never sends it. ## Skill Library Report **Analyze skill library** reviews your installed skills and prepares proposals, such as two skills with similar instructions. It prepares proposals for your review; nothing is applied. ## What Is Saved Insights and their proposals are local Row-Bot data. Applying a proposal changes only what that proposal names. ## Troubleshooting - If the feed is empty, Row-Bot has nothing to report yet; new insights appear after it analyses recent work. - If an action's outcome is not confirmed, use **Check outcome** before trying again.

## Phone And Native Desktop

Route: /docs/mobile-native/

Use the full Row-Bot owner product from a phone, connect it from Settings Devices & remote access, and understand native-only desktop behaviour.

# Phone And Native Desktop A phone connected to your Row-Bot gets the whole owner product in a layout made for a small screen: conversations, Home with Overview, Workflows, Knowledge, Monitor and Insights, approvals, and every Settings page. The native desktop app adds operating-system integration such as the window, tray, microphone, file and folder pickers, the terminal, and the updater. Layout never changes Row-Bot's authority or the approval rules of the underlying task. ## The Phone Layout Row-Bot switches to the phone layout when the window is narrow, whatever the device. - A slim top bar opens the sidebar as a drawer and opens the command palette. - In a conversation, the header's **** menu holds **Find in conversation**, **Conversation details**, **Share or export**, **Rename conversation**, the conversation's panels, and the command palette. - Design and Developer panels open as full-screen sheets. - Settings shows a **Settings section** list at the top instead of the side list. It holds every page, in the same six groups as on the desktop: Preferences, Appearance and Buddy; Providers, Models and Voice; Memory, Documents and Tracker; Tools and Skills; Apps, Accounts and Channels; System, Devices & remote access, Updates and Data. Features that need the computer running Row-Bot, such as the interactive terminal, choosing folders, and saving files with the system's Save dialog, are available only in the Row-Bot desktop app there. ## Connect A Phone 1. On the computer running Row-Bot, open **Settings Devices & remote access** and choose **Connect a phone or computer**. The command palette finds it as "phone". 2. Choose **How will it reach this computer?**: **Tailscale** (private and encrypted, recommended), **Same Wi-Fi** (at home or the office, over HTTP), **Internet** (from anywhere, through your public link), or another address you set up yourself. 3. Choose how long it should **Stay signed in**: **30 days** or **12 hours**. 4. **Scan the code** with the phone's camera, or open the shown address on it. 5. On the phone, review the connection page and press **Connect** before the code expires. 6. **Your devices** lists every signed-in phone and computer; sign one out when it is lost, replaced, or no longer trusted. The code expires after 10 minutes and works once. Opening it does not use it up until the phone presses **Connect**. The resulting session is a separate HttpOnly browser credential and never appears in the address. Connecting grants access to your local Row-Bot instance. Do not share a code, expose the local server broadly, or use Same Wi-Fi HTTP on an untrusted network. Tailscale or an operator-managed HTTPS address is preferred and is required for browser microphone use away from the computer. See [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access) for the complete connection and recovery model. ## Native-Only Checks Some states cannot be reproduced faithfully in browser automation: OS microphone prompts, native file and folder pickers, tray menus, updater and restart dialogs, Computer Use takeover, and physical-device network permission. The public guide documents their intent; release review must test them on the target operating system and a physical phone. ## Troubleshooting - If the phone cannot connect, check the route you chose on the computer, the port, the firewall, and whether both devices can reach each other. - If a code expired or was already used, show a new code rather than copying cookies or local credential files. - If the connection page opens but the app stays unavailable, confirm the phone pressed **Connect** and that the device wasn't signed out. - If an approval seems missing, open Overview: **Needs you** lists every waiting approval. - If the phone layout appears on a computer, widen the window; the layout follows the window's width.

## How Row-Bot Works

Route: /docs/concepts/

Understand Row-Bot's request, knowledge, agent, workflow, and extension models before configuring them.

# How Row-Bot Works These pages explain the ideas behind Row-Bot without walking through every control. Use them when you want to predict what the app will do, where data goes, why work continues in the background, or what an extension is allowed to change. - [How A Request Runs](/docs/concepts/request-lifecycle) follows a message from a thread through model context, tools, approvals, and saved results. - [How Memory Becomes Knowledge](/docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle) separates thread history, memory, documents, the Knowledge Graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle. - [How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work](/docs/concepts/profiles-goals-and-agents) explains reusable roles, durable objectives, parent coordination, and child-agent hand-offs. - [How Background Workflows Run](/docs/concepts/background-workflows) explains schedules, run state, approvals, retries, and delivery. - [Extensions And Trust Boundaries](/docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust) compares built-in tools, Skills, Custom Tools, plugins, MCP, channels, and accounts. Each page ends with links to the settings and task guides that change the behaviour it describes.

## How A Request Runs

Route: /docs/concepts/request-lifecycle

Follow a Row-Bot request through context assembly, a selected model route, tools, approvals, and local history.

# How A Request Runs A Row-Bot request is a controlled loop, not a single message sent blindly to every connected service. 1. **A thread provides continuity.** Your message joins the selected conversation. The thread supplies recent history and any thread-specific model or profile choice. 2. **Row-Bot assembles useful context.** Depending on your settings and request, this can include profile instructions, pinned or task-selected Skills, attachments, and relevant local memory or document results. Enabled skills that are not yet selected stay in a compact searchable catalog. It does not mean the whole local data directory is attached. 3. **The selected model route receives the model prompt.** A local model keeps that inference on the configured local runtime. A hosted, API, subscription, or remote custom endpoint sends the assembled prompt to that provider under its terms. 4. **The model may answer or ask for a tool.** Core tools are bound under the active profile. In Auto mode, Row-Bot can search enabled external MCP, plugin, Custom Tool, and channel capabilities when needed. It then checks that the selected tool is enabled, provider-compatible, and permitted by policy. 5. **Consequential actions stop at an approval boundary.** The approval describes the proposed action and target. Rejecting it prevents that action; approving it does not give unrelated future actions permission. 6. **Tool results return to the active run.** A local file tool, browser, channel, account, plugin, or MCP server has its own execution and data boundary. The model can use the result to continue the loop. 7. **The result is recorded locally.** The thread keeps the conversation and run evidence. Optional extraction, memory, and document features decide what becomes reusable knowledge later. ## Three Boundaries To Keep In Mind | Boundary | What crosses it | What controls it | | --- | --- | --- | | Model route | The assembled prompt and later tool results needed for reasoning. | Selected provider/model, thread override, profile or workflow policy. | | Tool execution | Arguments needed by a local or external capability. | Tool enablement, workspace or account scope, approval policy. | | Durable knowledge | Reviewed or extracted information that may be recalled in another request. | Memory, Knowledge, document, embedding, and retention settings. | Local-first describes where Row-Bot and its durable data live. It does not make a hosted model, web tool, channel, remote MCP server, realtime voice provider, or external account local. ## Change How Requests Run - Choose routes and defaults in [Models And Providers](/docs/configuration/models-and-providers), [Provider Settings](/docs/settings/providers), and [Model Settings](/docs/settings/models). - Control tools and approvals in [Tools, Approvals, And Terminal](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal) and [Privacy And Safety](/docs/privacy-safety/). - Control reusable context in [Memory Settings](/docs/settings/knowledge), [Documents Settings](/docs/settings/documents), and [Skills Settings](/docs/settings/skills). - Configure automatic or eager external capability loading in [Tools Settings](/docs/settings/tools) and read [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills).

## How Memory Becomes Knowledge

Route: /docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle

Understand thread history, memory, documents, the Knowledge Graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle as related but distinct layers.

# How Memory Becomes Knowledge Row-Bot has several kinds of continuity. They work together, but none is a magical copy of everything the app has ever seen. | Layer | What it represents | How it is used | | --- | --- | --- | | Thread history | Messages, attachments, tool traces, approvals, and results in one conversation. | Keeps the current conversation coherent and reviewable. | | Memory | Reusable facts, preferences, summaries, and events saved or extracted for later recall. | Supplies selected relevant context to future requests when enabled. | | Documents | Files deliberately added to the document library and split into searchable content. | Finds passages related to a question without placing every document in every prompt. | | Knowledge Graph | Local entities and directed relationships with source and confidence information. | Connects related people, projects, events, facts, and sources during review and recall. | | Wiki Vault | Linked Markdown pages generated from reviewed graph material. | Makes a portable, human-browsable projection in a folder you choose. | ## From Conversation To Recall When extraction is enabled, Row-Bot can identify useful information from eligible conversations or documents and save structured records. Search combines the available lexical, vector, and graph signals to choose candidates relevant to a later request. Recall refreshes useful memories; it does not make every stored item equally likely to appear. Vector search uses an embedding model, which is separate from the chat model. The recommended local one is Mixedbread Embed Large v1, a 675 MB download you install from Settings Documents. Until it is installed, or while it is unavailable or still loading, Row-Bot continues with bounded lexical and graph fallback instead of silently downloading during a chat. Install, retry, or repair the local model later in [Documents Settings](/docs/settings/documents), then rebuild document and memory vectors after changing models. Cloud embeddings are an explicit alternative that sends indexed text to the selected provider. The source record matters. A graph relation or memory should remain traceable to the conversation, document, or process that produced it. Correct the underlying Knowledge record before rebuilding derived indexes or Wiki Vault pages. ## What Dream Cycle Does Dream Cycle is idle-time knowledge maintenance. When enabled and due, it can examine the local knowledge set, merge high-confidence duplicates, refresh summaries from available source context, infer strongly supported relationships, and prune stale low-confidence inferred relations. It records its history so you can review what happened in Monitor. Dream Cycle is not an autonomous second assistant and it does not make external facts true. It should run only during the configured window while the app is idle. Inferred relationships use confidence thresholds, but important knowledge still deserves human review. ## What Wiki Vault Does Wiki Vault writes a readable view of selected graph material. The graph remains the source of truth; the vault is a generated output. If the destination is synced to a cloud drive, repository, or publishing tool, that folder becomes a separate sharing boundary. ## Configure And Review It - Review memories in [Knowledge](/docs/knowledge/) (Home Knowledge) and investigate changes in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/). - Turn memory on or off, check graph health and configure Wiki output in [Memory Settings](/docs/settings/knowledge); Dream Cycle's hours are in Settings Preferences. - Configure indexed files in [Documents Settings](/docs/settings/documents). - Set up the export folder in [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault) and correct mistakes with [Provenance And Repair](/docs/knowledge/provenance-repair). - Back up the related local data as one set using [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/).

## How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work

Route: /docs/concepts/profiles-goals-and-agents

Understand reusable Agent Profiles, durable goals, parent coordination, and bounded child-agent delegation.

# How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work Profiles, goals, and agent runs describe different parts of long-running work. - An **Agent Profile** is a reusable operating role: instructions, model policy, Skills, tools, delegation limits, and approval policy. - A **goal** is the durable objective and finish condition for a piece of work that may span several turns. - An **agent run** is one execution attempt with a prompt, model, status, result, and evidence. - A **parent agent** coordinates the objective and combines results. - A **child agent** receives a bounded subtask and returns a hand-off to its parent. ## Why Delegate Delegation is useful when independent research, inspection, or implementation can happen in parallel or needs a specialist profile. It is less useful when agents would edit the same small resource or when only one decision is needed. The parent remains responsible for deciding whether the combined evidence actually completes the goal. Child agents do not become invisible background permissions. Their runs remain linked to the parent, and a returned result is evidence rather than automatic authorisation to write, send, publish, or declare the goal complete. Tool availability and approvals still apply to the run doing the action. Delegation capacity is bounded. Each new run snapshots the application-wide work-round, nesting, per-parent concurrency, app-wide concurrency, and optional child active-time settings. When capacity is full, eligible children wait in a first-in, first-out queue rather than bypassing the limits. ## Status And Hand-Offs An active goal can accumulate progress across turns, with no turn limit unless you set one. After each turn Row-Bot judges whether the goal made progress, is done, or is blocked; two turns without progress, or the same step failing three times, pause it with the reason so you can decide. Completion should mean the finish condition and required checks are satisfied. A block should identify a real impasse, not merely unfinished work. Stopping an agent ends that run without deleting the parent thread, goal history, or already-recorded evidence. The work-round budget is checked at model, tool, and resume boundaries so a restart cannot reset it. Repeated no-progress states are blocked and then terminated cleanly, and every terminal path writes one durable final status and reason. A useful child-agent hand-off says what was checked, what changed, what evidence was found, what remains uncertain, and whether any consequential action still needs the parent or user. ## Configure And Use It - Create and select roles, set goals and follow delegated agents with [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/). - Choose a profile in a workflow with [Workflows](/docs/guides/workflows). - Control the models behind runs in [Models And Providers](/docs/configuration/models-and-providers). - Review waiting work and failures in [Home: Overview](/docs/home/overview) or [Monitor](/docs/monitor/).

## How Background Workflows Run

Route: /docs/concepts/background-workflows

Understand saved workflow definitions, schedules, isolated runs, approvals, retries, and delivery semantics.

# How Background Workflows Run A workflow is a saved task definition. A run is one attempt to execute it. Keeping those separate lets Row-Bot preserve history when you edit the next schedule or retry a failed attempt. 1. **A trigger starts a run.** This can be a manual click, a recurring schedule, a one-time time, or another supported trigger. 2. **The run resolves its policy.** Row-Bot chooses the workflow's Agent Profile, model override, tools, Skills, steps, and approval mode. 3. **The run gets its own state.** Status, progress, step output, logs, and any persistent thread link are recorded so the scheduler can recover cleanly. 4. **Approval can pause the run.** A background action that needs a decision becomes a pending approval instead of silently continuing. It waits until you answer, unless a step sets its own time limit, and it shows everywhere: the sidebar's attention indicator, Overview's **Needs you**, Buddy, and the workflow's channels. Approving resumes that action; denying it leaves a visible run outcome. While a run waits, the same workflow's next scheduled run is skipped and says so, so runs don't pile up. 5. **Completion and delivery are recorded separately.** A useful result can complete even if an external channel delivery fails, so the app can show the result and the delivery problem honestly. ## Delivery Defaults The web app always receives run status. External channels are an additional destination. - **Inherit defaults** means the workflow uses the current workflow-level external channel selection. - **An explicit empty selection** means web app only, even when a global external default exists. - **An explicit channel selection** targets those configured running channels. This distinction prevents a workflow that was deliberately set to app-only from beginning to send externally after someone changes the global default. ## Failure And Retry A failed run remains evidence; retrying creates another attempt rather than rewriting history. Fix the underlying provider, model, tool, approval, input, or delivery problem first. For multi-step work, keep steps narrow enough that the status identifies where the run stopped. Scheduled work can outlive the screen where it was created, but it cannot outlive the local Row-Bot process indefinitely. Pausing a workflow prevents future schedule starts; stopping one active run does not necessarily change the saved schedule. ## Configure And Operate It - Create schedules, profiles, approvals, steps, and delivery in [Workflows](/docs/guides/workflows). - Configure external destinations in [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels); each channel is an app in [Settings Apps](/docs/settings/apps#built-in-ways-to-connect). - Review live status in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/) and waiting approvals in [Home: Overview](/docs/home/overview), on the desktop or a [phone](/docs/mobile-native/). - Back up workflow definitions and history with [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/).

## Extensions And Trust Boundaries

Route: /docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust

Compare Row-Bot tools, Skills, Custom Tools, plugins, MCP servers, channels, and accounts by what they add and where they run.

# Extensions And Trust Boundaries Row-Bot can learn a procedure, gain a tool, load code, connect a server, or authorise an account. Those are different changes and deserve different review. | Capability | What it adds | Main trust question | | --- | --- | --- | | Built-in tool | A maintained capability shipped with Row-Bot. | Is it enabled for this profile, and does this action need approval? | | Skill | Instructions, examples, and supporting files that shape behaviour. | Do the instructions match your intent and avoid unexpected data or tool use? | | Custom Tool | Reviewed local code or a command exposed as a reusable tool. | What code runs, in which workspace, with which dependencies and command class? | | Plugin (package) | A packaged extension that can add code, tools, Skills, apps, configuration, or UI. | Do you trust its publisher, source, permissions, dependencies, and update path? | | App | Tools from a hosted service, or from a program that runs on this computer. | What can it access, where does it run, and what may it do without asking? | | Channel | A bridge for incoming messages or outgoing results. | Who can contact it, which conversation receives replies, and may workflows deliver there? | | Account | Authorisation for a service such as GitHub, Google, or X. | Which service scopes and account data become available to enabled tools? | ## Instructions Are Not Permissions A Skill or profile can tell the model when to use a capability, but it does not create credentials or bypass Row-Bot's tool and approval policy. Conversely, connecting an app or adding a package can add real executable capability even when no Skill mentions it. Review both the guidance layer and the execution layer. When you connect an app, you choose what it may do: **Read only**, **Ask before changes** (the default) or **Full access**. Deleting, sending, paying, publishing, running code and unknown actions always ask, whichever you choose; Full access only lets routine changes run without asking. Progressive discovery preserves this separation. Loading a skill adds instructions to one task; it cannot make a profile-denied tool callable. Searching an enabled external-tool catalog does not enable a tool, change its provider schema, or bypass its approval classification. ## Local Does Not Always Mean Harmless A local plugin, command, or MCP process can still read files, start programs, or use locally stored credentials. A remote server or account can send data outside the app even if its configuration is stored locally. Use narrow workspaces, least-privilege accounts, disabled-by-default imports, and fictional test data. Third-party dependency telemetry is not Row-Bot telemetry. Review dependency behaviour before installation and do not expose prompts, files, memories, secrets, screenshots, tool arguments, or channel content unless that transfer is the feature you intentionally selected. ## Browse And Configure Extensions - Compare extension types and browse screenshots in [Extend Row-Bot](/docs/extending/). - Browse and review Skills in [Skills](/docs/skills/) and [Skills Settings](/docs/settings/skills). - Understand automatic capability selection in [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills) and configure it in [Tools Settings](/docs/settings/tools). - Find, connect, and choose access for apps and packages in [Apps Settings](/docs/settings/apps), with background in [Hosted And Local Apps](/docs/integrations/mcp) and [Packages](/docs/integrations/plugins). - Configure external messaging in [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels) and service authorisation in [Accounts And Authorisation](/docs/integrations/accounts).

## Settings

Route: /docs/settings/

Find every Row-Bot settings page: six groups from General to System, with search for any setting.

# Settings Settings is where Row-Bot is configured: where models come from and which one does each job, memory and documents, tools, skills and apps (your accounts and messaging channels included), and how Row-Bot runs on this computer and your other devices. Open it with **Settings** at the bottom of the sidebar. The pages are grouped down the left side; **Find a setting** (press / on a Settings page) searches page names and individual settings and jumps to the exact row. The command palette finds them too, and can flip common switches in place. On a phone, a **Settings section** list at the top replaces the side list; every page and setting is still there. ## How Settings Is Organized | Group | Page | What it changes | | --- | --- | --- | | **General** | [Preferences](/docs/settings/preferences) | The assistant's name and personality, learning new skills, how Row-Bot opens, and the overnight Dream Cycle. | | | [Appearance](/docs/settings/preferences#appearance) | Theme, accent colour, density and transparency on this device, and panel sizes. | | | [Buddy](/docs/settings/buddy) | Your companion's look, personality and motion, and the desktop overlay. | | **Models** | [Providers](/docs/settings/providers) | Where models come from: local, subscription, pay-per-use and custom endpoints. | | | [Models](/docs/settings/models) | Which model does each job (Brain, Vision, Image, Video), limits for long work, and the catalog. | | | [Voice](/docs/settings/voice) | Talk, dictation and read-aloud. | | **Knowledge** | [Memory](/docs/settings/knowledge) | Remembering on or off, graph health and the wiki vault. Memories themselves live in Home Knowledge. | | | [Documents](/docs/settings/documents) | Files Row-Bot can search, and where search runs. | | | [Tracker](/docs/settings/tracker) | Habits, symptoms and health events you track. | | **Capabilities** | [Tools](/docs/settings/tools) | Capability loading, retrieval compression, search tools, built-in tools and custom tools. | | | [Skills](/docs/settings/skills) | Find, add, try and remove skills, and create or edit your own. | | **Connections** | [Apps](/docs/settings/apps) | The services Row-Bot can work in, including the GitHub, Google (Gmail and Calendar) and X accounts and the Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack and SMS channels: find, connect, choose what each may do, change settings, turn off and remove. | | **System** | [System](/docs/settings/system) | The workspace folder, what Row-Bot may do (commands, files, browser and computer use), and logs. | | | [Devices & remote access](/docs/operations/remote-access) | Connect a phone or computer, your signed-in devices, network access and the public link. | | | [Updates](/docs/operations/#update-repair-and-uninstall) | The version you have, the update channel, and checking for updates. | | | [Data](/docs/operations/#back-up) | Back up and restore, import from another assistant, and irreversible clean-up. | Goals belong to one conversation and are set in its details card; agent profiles are managed in the sidebar's **Agents** dialog. See [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/). All authenticated owner sessions see the same settings on every device. On phones and tablets, the layout adapts to the screen; the available settings and authority do not change. ## A Good Setup Order 1. Providers 2. Models 3. Documents and Tools 4. Skills 5. System access 6. Apps, including your accounts and channels 7. Voice and Buddy 8. Preferences and Appearance Accounts and channels used to have their own Settings pages; they are apps now. Old links open the matching app. ## Safety Notes Credentials belong in Providers or in an app's setup in Apps (accounts and channels included), not in chat messages. Turn on only the tools and apps you intend to use. Review approvals before actions that write files, run commands, use accounts, contact external services, or send messages.

## Settings: Providers

Route: /docs/settings/providers

Connect local, hosted, subscription, and custom model providers.

# Settings: Providers Providers are the model services Row-Bot can call. This page answers whether each provider is connected, what kind of credential it uses, and whether Row-Bot has enough information to use it for chat, tools, designs, code, voice, or embeddings. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Providers** in the **Models** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Controls - Connection Status summarizes how many providers are connected, local, API-based, subscription-based, or media-capable. - Local providers show runtimes such as Ollama. Refresh checks what the local service currently exposes. - Subscription accounts show sign-in based providers such as ChatGPT / Codex or Claude Subscription. Use connect, reconnect, test, and refresh actions from the row. - API providers show services that need an API key or compatible endpoint. Their credential buttons open the setup flow for that provider. - xAI API catalog refresh also discovers live image-generation models and their supported output formats, aspect ratios, resolutions, and quality choices. Row-Bot keeps that capability metadata separate from ordinary chat models. - Custom endpoint providers let advanced users point Row-Bot at OpenAI-compatible servers such as LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI, LiteLLM, or SGLang. - Custom endpoint Advanced settings can describe reasoning mode, a thinking budget, returned reasoning content, and whether preserved reasoning may be replayed to that endpoint. - Runtime tests check whether a provider can handle the kind of requests Row-Bot needs. A failed test keeps the provider visible but may stop Row-Bot from offering it for agent work. ## Common Workflow 1. Pick one provider path first: local Ollama for private local runs, a subscription account if you already use one, or an API provider if you prefer hosted models. 2. Add credentials or sign in only through the provider row you intend to use. 3. Refresh the provider so Row-Bot can discover available models. 4. Open **Settings Models** to choose which model does each job and pin the ones you use most. ## What Is Saved Provider connection state is global to the local Row-Bot app. Secrets are stored in the operating system key store when available; Row-Bot settings keep masked status and catalog metadata. ## Privacy And Safety Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#providers-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If a provider is connected but models do not appear, refresh Providers, then refresh Models. - If an xAI image model is missing or rejects a media option, refresh Providers so Row-Bot can use the live image-generation catalog. A quality choice that the endpoint rejects is retried once without that optional field; other generation failures are returned without an automatic duplicate request. - If a runtime test fails, read the row message before changing credentials; the model may be chat-capable but not tool-capable. - If local Ollama is missing, start Ollama and make sure at least one model is installed.

## Settings: Models

Route: /docs/settings/models

Choose which model does each job (Brain, Vision, Image, Video), set the reading limit and limits for long work, and pin models from the catalog.

# Settings: Models The Models page decides which model does each job. Providers supply the models (see [Settings: Providers](/docs/settings/providers)); this page picks between them. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Models** in the **Models** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Jobs Each job has its own picker, using the same grouped, searchable list as the composer's model picker (provider, how it is paid for, and whether it is available): - **Brain** is the default model for new conversations and background work. A conversation can still choose its own model in the composer. - **Vision** reads images, screenshots and your camera. Leave it as **Same as Brain** if your Brain model can see, or choose another model. Choose a **Camera** here too. - **Image** makes and edits pictures. - **Video** makes short clips and animates pictures. Turn Vision, Image or Video off when you don't want that job done at all. ## Reading Limit **Reading limit** sets how much text the Brain model reads at once. **Automatic** uses what the model supports; **Limit...** sets a smaller number of tokens, useful for local models on smaller computers. ## Limits For Long Work These limits apply to new runs; work in progress keeps the limits it started with. **Recommended limits** restores the defaults. | Limit | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **Steps per run** | Model-and-tool rounds one run may take. | | **Helper levels** | How deep delegation goes; 1 lets helpers work but not start helpers of their own. | | **Helpers at a time, per agent** | Delegated agents one agent runs at once; more wait in line. | | **Helpers at a time, in total** | Delegated agents running across the whole app. | | **Helper time limit (seconds)** | How long one helper may work; 0 means no limit, and time waiting in line doesn't count. | | **Goal turn limit** | The turn limit new goals start with; 0, the default, means no limit. Each goal can change it. | ## Catalog The **Catalog** lists every model your providers offer. Search it, filter by provider and job, and pin the models you use often so they appear first in every picker. **Refresh catalog** asks your providers what is available now. ## Common Workflow 1. Connect a provider, then choose your **Brain** model. 2. Choose Vision, Image and Video models if you want those jobs. 3. Pin one everyday model and one stronger tool-capable model. 4. Keep the recommended limits unless you have a measured reason to change them. ## What Is Saved Job models, limits and pins are global preferences. A conversation keeps its own model when you choose one in it. ## Privacy And Safety A hosted model receives the prompts, images or files its job sends it. Choose local models for jobs that should stay on your computer. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#models-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If a picker is empty, connect a provider first. - If a model is missing, refresh the catalog and check whether its provider is connected. - If a model shows as unavailable, read its reason; reconnecting its provider usually fixes it. - If a small local model fails before answering, lower the reading limit or choose a more capable model.

## Settings: Memory

Route: /docs/settings/knowledge

Turn remembering on or off, check graph health, configure the wiki vault, and delete all knowledge in Settings Memory.

# Settings: Memory The Memory page holds the settings for what Row-Bot remembers between conversations. The memories themselves are in **Home Knowledge**, where you search, review, edit and delete them. See [Knowledge](/docs/knowledge/). ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Memory** in the **Knowledge** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. Old links to Settings Knowledge or Settings Wiki open this page. ## Remembering **Enable Memory** decides whether Row-Bot saves useful facts from conversations and recalls them later. A link opens Home Knowledge to manage what is saved. ## Graph Health **Graph health** counts your **Memories**, how many **Connected groups** they form, and how many **Unconnected memories** stand alone. A memory graph thumbnail opens Home Knowledge. Many unconnected memories usually means Dream Cycle or a review would help. ## Wiki Vault **Wiki vault** writes your memories as linked Markdown articles in a folder you choose, and brings your edits back. See [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault). ## Delete All Knowledge **Delete all knowledge** permanently removes the saved graph after reviewing exactly what will go. Row-Bot-managed wiki files and local indexes are cleaned up; files outside Row-Bot's managed wiki are kept. Back up first if you might want it back. ## Related Settings - Dream Cycle's hours are in **Settings Preferences Overnight tidy-up**. - Where memory and document search runs, and its search model, are in **Settings Documents**. ## Common Workflow 1. Keep memory on if you want Row-Bot to remember useful details. 2. Install the private search model in Settings Documents before building a large memory. 3. Review and correct important memories in Home Knowledge. 4. Turn on the wiki vault when you want a readable local copy outside the app. ## What Is Saved Memories live in local Row-Bot data. They are sent to a model provider only as relevant context in a conversation that uses that provider. ## Privacy And Safety The wiki vault is a folder other software can read or sync; treat it as an export. Deleting all knowledge cannot be undone without a backup. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#memory-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If recall feels stale, rebuild the memory index in Settings Documents. - If Row-Bot remembers something wrong, edit or archive the memory in Home Knowledge. - If Dream Cycle is noisy, change its hours or turn it off in Settings Preferences.

## Settings: Buddy

Route: /docs/settings/buddy

Use Buddy in the sidebar or as a compact desktop overlay, message the selected thread, handle approvals, and configure its appearance.

# Settings: Buddy Buddy is Row-Bot's visual companion. It starts in the sidebar and, in the native Windows and macOS apps, can be dragged out into a compact always-on-top desktop overlay. The overlay is a smaller view of the thread selected in Row-Bot: it uses that thread's model, tools, approval mode, saved draft, and conversation rather than starting a separate assistant. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Buddy** in the **General** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Undock Buddy Onto The Desktop 1. Turn on **Show Buddy** if the companion is hidden. 2. Press and drag Buddy itself away from its sidebar dock. Releasing it back over the dock cancels the move; dragging it beyond the native Row-Bot window tears it off. 3. Drop it near the part of the desktop where you want the overlay. Row-Bot keeps the fixed-size overlay inside the nearest monitor's usable work area, including multi-monitor layouts. 4. Drag the overlay header whenever you want to reposition it. Drag-to-undock requires the native Windows or macOS application. Browser/server mode, Linux browser-first launch, and the phone layout keep Buddy inside Row-Bot and do not create a native overlay window. ## Message The Selected Thread The title at the top of the overlay identifies the thread that will receive your next message. Buddy follows the conversation selected in the main Row-Bot window: switch conversations there and Buddy switches with you. The smaller line shows whether that thread is a Chat, Code, or Design conversation and what it is doing. If no thread is selected, Buddy follows your most recent conversation. - Type into **Message this thread...**. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. - The full composer and overlay share the saved draft for each thread. Switching threads loads that thread's draft without merging it into another conversation. - Sending captures the thread and the Chat, Code, or Design context shown at that moment, so changing the main-window selection during a run does not silently retarget the request. - After sending, the overlay shows current progress, the latest response, or an error. If a response was interrupted (for example by a restart), **Resume** continues it. - Use **Stop** to stop the selected thread's active response. The overlay does not retry the turn by itself. - Attachments, transcript history, tool traces, model selection, and microphone controls remain in the full Row-Bot thread. Use **Open full thread** when you need them. The overlay is a text composer, not a second microphone session. Talk and Dictate remain in the full thread. A voice turn submitted there belongs to the same conversation and its progress can still appear in Buddy. ## Review Approvals Buddy never creates a separate approval policy. It projects the selected thread's existing gate: - The current approval shows **Deny**, **Details**, and **Approve** in the overlay. Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) approves. - **Details** opens the full thread so you can inspect the complete request before deciding. - If the selected thread or pending generation no longer matches, Buddy opens the full thread instead of approving a stale request. ## Overlay Menu And Lifecycle - **Open full thread** restores the main Row-Bot window at the selected conversation. - **Dock Buddy** closes the native overlay and returns Buddy to its sidebar dock. - **Hide Buddy** hides the overlay without docking it. Use the tray's **Show Buddy** action to bring it back. - While Buddy is torn off, closing the main Row-Bot window hides that window instead of quitting the app. Use **Open full thread**, **Open Row-Bot** in the tray, or the tray's quit action as appropriate. - Tear-off is session-scoped. A fresh Row-Bot launch resets placement to the sidebar dock; a saved hidden preference remains hidden until you show Buddy. - The overlay follows Row-Bot's appearance setting (System, Light, or Dark) and your device's reduced-motion setting. ## Appearance Controls The Buddy page follows the conversation you have open, because Buddy uses that conversation's profile and approvals; open a conversation first if it asks. - **Show Buddy** shows or hides the companion. - **Look** chooses a bundled or custom Buddy appearance. **New look...** makes one with your image model; **Refresh looks** reads them again. - **Personality** changes the tone of Buddy's status cues. - **Bubbles** changes how visual status appears. - **Motion** chooses how lively Buddy is: **Calm**, **Normal** or **Lively**. - **Advanced Buddy settings** holds Buddy's **Name**, optional **Style notes** for new looks, and **Compact size**. Buddy's picture is also the speaker mark beside Row-Bot's replies in conversations. ## Common Workflow 1. Select the thread you want and confirm its name in the main window. 2. Drag Buddy out of the sidebar and confirm the same name appears in the overlay header. 3. Type a short message, review any approval, and use **Open full thread** when you need the complete transcript or tool details. 4. Use **Dock Buddy** when you want it back in the sidebar. 5. Make a new look only after an image model is ready in Settings Models; choose **Calm** motion if animation is distracting. ## What Is Saved Buddy visibility, appearance, overlay position, and thread drafts are local app data. The overlay does not copy conversations into a second store. Generating a custom look may call a configured media provider depending on your setup. ## Privacy And Safety The overlay follows the same privacy and safety boundaries as the selected thread. A hosted model, tool, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or media provider can still send data externally when that thread uses it. Undocking Buddy does not grant new permissions or bypass approvals. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#buddy-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If Buddy does not appear in the sidebar, turn on **Show Buddy** and reload the current page if needed. - If a drag snaps back, start the gesture on Buddy itself and release away from the original dock. Drag-to-undock is unavailable outside the native Windows and macOS apps. - If a hidden overlay is still torn off, use **Show Buddy** from the system tray. - If Row-Bot's main window is hidden, use **Open Row-Bot** from the tray or **Open full thread** from Buddy. - If the overlay shows the wrong conversation, select the intended thread in Row-Bot and verify the overlay title before sending. - If an approval needs more context, choose **Review** or **Details** and decide in the full thread. - Restart Row-Bot to reset desktop placement to the sidebar dock. Then enable **Show Buddy** if a saved hidden preference keeps it out of view. - If making a new look fails, check that an image model is chosen and its provider is connected.

## Settings: Voice

Route: /docs/settings/voice

Configure dictation, realtime talk, read-aloud, voice models, devices, and diagnostics.

# Settings: Voice Voice gives Row-Bot microphone input and optional spoken output. Dictate turns speech into text for the composer. Talk is a conversation mode. Realtime voice uses a low-latency provider path when configured. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Voice** in the **Models** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Controls - Talk settings decide whether spoken input submits directly to Row-Bot. - Dictate settings decide whether speech is inserted into the composer for review before sending. - Read-aloud settings control spoken assistant responses. - Local voice controls choose Whisper, the default local STT engine, or the optional FunASR/SenseVoice engine for Talk and Dictate. - SenseVoice readiness shows whether the platform, packaged runtime, and verified local model snapshot are ready. Its install action is always explicit. - Realtime voice controls use provider-backed low-latency voice models. - Device controls select microphone and output devices. - Voice Models shows runtime defaults and provider voice models. - Diagnostics checks local audio and provider readiness. Talk and Dictate controls live in the full chat composer, not the compact Buddy desktop overlay. If Buddy is undocked, use **Open full thread** before starting a microphone session; Buddy will continue to reflect the selected thread's response and approval state. ## Common Workflow 1. Use Dictate first if you want to review text before sending. 2. Use Talk when you want hands-light conversation and are comfortable with immediate submission. 3. Choose local Whisper for the default local path, or install and select SenseVoice Small when you want the optional FunASR engine. 4. Treat the SenseVoice install as a deliberate approximately 940 MB ModelScope download. After verification, normal transcription stays local and cache-only. 5. Choose realtime voice when latency matters and you accept provider requirements, cost, and internet use. ## What Is Saved Voice preferences are global. Transcribed text belongs to the active thread once submitted. The verified SenseVoice snapshot is stored under the active Row-Bot data directory. Provider-backed voice can send audio or transcript data to the selected provider. ## Privacy And Safety Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere. The explicit SenseVoice install contacts ModelScope for the model download; it does not send audio, prompts, or usage data, and ordinary inference does not check for updates. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#voice-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If the microphone is silent, check the selected input device and browser/app permissions. - If SenseVoice is missing or invalid, use its install or reinstall action in Voice settings. Source installs also require the `voice` extra. - SenseVoice is unavailable on Intel macOS because the required CPU PyTorch and Torchaudio wheels are not published for that runtime; use local Whisper there. - If realtime voice is unavailable, configure a compatible provider in Providers. - If Talk submits too quickly, use Dictate mode instead.

## Settings: System

Route: /docs/settings/system

Choose Row-Bot's workspace folder and what it may do on this computer (commands, files, browser and computer use), and manage logs.

# Settings: System System settings describe where Row-Bot works on this computer and what it may do there: run commands, work with files, drive a browser, and, if you opt in, operate desktop apps with Computer Use. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **System** in the **System** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Workspace **Workspace folder** is where Row-Bot keeps its own files on this computer, such as new draft code folders. Choosing a folder needs the Row-Bot desktop app. ## What Row-Bot May Do Risky actions still ask first, as each conversation's **Approvals** setting decides. - **Run commands** turns the shell tool on or off. The command palette can flip it too ("turn off shell"). - **Work with files** controls the file tools. - **Browser and computer use** opens their setup: - **Browser** turns the browser tool on and chooses its runtime: a supported installed Chrome or Edge, or Row-Bot's exact managed Playwright Chromium. **Install browser runtime** and Repair are explicit actions; normal start-up only checks readiness and never downloads a browser. - **Desktop apps** sets up **Computer Use (Beta)**, which stays off by default and is gated by platform readiness, its telemetry disclosure, and a verified optional runtime. See [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use/). ## Logs **Log detail** sets how much Row-Bot writes to its local log. **Open log folder** opens it. Monitor's **Logs** shows the same log inside the app. ## Advanced System Settings Additional blocked command patterns, app availability for Computer Use, and removing the managed Computer Use runtime live under **Advanced system settings**. ## What Moved - Connecting a phone or another computer, signed-in devices, network access and the public link (tunnel) are on **Settings Devices & remote access**. See [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access). - **Open in** (app window or browser) is on **Settings Preferences**. - Updates are on **Settings Updates**. ## Common Workflow 1. Keep the workspace folder somewhere you back up. 2. Turn on commands, files or the browser only when you intend to use those tools. 3. Turn on Computer Use only on an interactive Windows or macOS desktop after reading its setup and safety guide. 4. Raise **Log detail** while troubleshooting, then lower it again. ## What Is Saved System settings are global for the active Row-Bot data directory. Workspace files are not uploaded to Row-Bot; external providers may still receive content when a model or tool request sends it. ## Privacy And Safety Commands, file access, browser automation and Computer Use widen what Row-Bot can do on this computer. Keep approvals on **Ask** in conversations that use them, and review each request. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#system-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If Row-Bot cannot read a file, check whether it is inside the folder it was given and that **Work with files** is on. - If Browser reports a missing or mismatched managed runtime, use **Install browser runtime** or Repair. Do not copy another Playwright cache into Row-Bot's managed location. - If Computer Use is unavailable, open its setup and follow the reported runtime or operating-system permission step. - If choosing the workspace folder does nothing, use the Row-Bot desktop app.

## Settings: Tracker

Route: /docs/settings/tracker

Configure recurring activity, habit, symptom, and health tracking surfaces.

# Settings: Tracker Tracker is for structured personal logs such as recurring activities, habits, symptoms, or health events. It gives Row-Bot a more organized way to store and review repeated observations than free-form chat alone. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Tracker** in the **Knowledge** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Controls - Category controls decide what kinds of events can be logged. - View and chart options change how tracker history is summarized. - Import or cleanup actions manage existing tracker data. - Privacy-oriented status text explains that tracker records stay in local app data unless you ask a provider or channel to use them. ## Common Workflow 1. Choose the categories you actually want to track. 2. Log events consistently from Chat or tracker-aware workflows. 3. Review trends in the tracker view before asking Row-Bot to summarize them. 4. Remove categories you no longer use to keep prompts focused. ## What Is Saved Tracker data is local Row-Bot data. It can influence answers only when Row-Bot is allowed to retrieve or summarize it. ## Privacy And Safety Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#tracker-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If a chart is empty, confirm there are saved events in that category. - If a summary seems wrong, inspect the raw tracker entries first. - If privacy matters, do not include tracker details in prompts sent to hosted providers.

## Settings: Documents

Route: /docs/settings/documents

Manage document ingestion, extraction, and vector indexing.

# Settings: Documents Documents let Row-Bot search files you add to its local document library. This is different from attaching a file to one chat: indexed documents become reusable context for future questions. Mixedbread Embed Large v1 is the recommended local embedding model; it is separate from the chat model and normal use loads it only from Row-Bot's private cache. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Documents** in the **Knowledge** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Controls - **Search runs** chooses where search works: **This computer** (your documents never leave it) or **Cloud** (document text goes to the embedding provider). Switching to Cloud asks first. - **Search model** chooses the embedding model. Mixedbread Embed Large v1 is the recommended local one. - **Free memory when idle** releases the local search model's memory after heavy document work. - **Index health and maintenance** shows the state of your document vectors and memory index: - **Dimension override** is for advanced embedding models that need a specific vector size. - **Document vectors** and **Memory index** each offer **Rebuild**, which recreates them with the current search settings. - **Search model files** offers **Download** to install the selected local model, **Retry** to load an already cached copy again, and **Repair** to replace a damaged download. Download and Repair need network access. - **Upload documents** adds files to Row-Bot-managed storage for indexing. - **Your documents** lists what Row-Bot has processed, with each document's status and progress, and can remove a document after review. ## Common Workflow 1. Under **Search model files**, choose **Download** before adding a large document library. 2. Upload a small test document and wait until it is indexed. 3. Ask a question in a chat that should require the document. 4. Rebuild vectors only when you change the search model or suspect stale results. ## What Is Saved Uploaded files, extracted text, vectors, and local embedding model caches are stored under the active Row-Bot data directory. In Docker, the named /data volume preserves the cache. The active chat only sees relevant results when document search is enabled. A cloud embedding provider is opt-in and sends indexed text to that provider; the recommended local model does not. ## Privacy And Safety Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere. ## Control-Level Reference The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#documents-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes. ## Troubleshooting - If search misses obvious content, rebuild vectors and check the embedding provider. - If the local model is missing, use **Download** under **Search model files**. Use **Retry** for a cached model or **Repair** for a damaged download. - If local indexing uses too much memory, turn on **Free memory when idle**. - If a document contains private material, remove it from the document library before sharing screenshots or logs.

## Settings: Tools

Route: /docs/settings/tools

Configure progressive external-tool loading, retrieval compression, search and knowledge tools, built-in tools, and custom tools.

# Settings: Tools Tools settings control how Row-Bot exposes enabled external capabilities to the model, its search and retrieval helpers, the small built-in tools it can use, and the custom tools you add. ## Where To Find It Open **Settings**, then choose **Tools** in the **Capabilities** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. ## Capability Loading - **Auto-select external tools (recommended)** lets Row-Bot search enabled MCP, plugin, Custom Tool, and channel capabilities when a request needs them. Core tools remain available under the active profile. - **Load all external tools** is the eager compatibility mode. It sends every enabled external schema allowed by the current provider and policy, which can consume more context. Both modes preserve tool enablement, provider compatibility, Agent Profile restrictions, workspace policy, approval gates, prompt-injection handling, and execution budgets. ## Other Controls - **Retrieval compression** controls how search results are filtered before they reach the model. - **Search & Knowledge Tools** enables or disables configured research and reference tools such as arXiv, DuckDuckGo, web search, Wikipedia, Wolfram Alpha, and YouTube. Provider-specific setup fields store the credentials required by optional search services. ## Built-In Tools **Built-in tools** are small tools for everyday tasks, such as the calculator, weather, charts and the URL reader. Each has its own switch, and the heading counts how many are on. These used to be a separate Utilities page. Developer tools are among them; the command palette can turn them on ("turn on developer tools"). ## Custom Tools **Custom tools** turns a folder's scripts into tools Row-Bot can run. **Add from a folder** (in the desktop app) inspects the folder and drafts the tool; this sends short excerpts of the folder to your chosen model, which may cost money with a paid provider. You can also ask Row-Bot in a chat to make a tool from a repository, or use the Custom Tool Builder in a code folder's Developer panel. Review a custom tool's commands before turning it on. ## Recommended Workflow 1. Keep **Auto-select external tools** enabled for normal use. 2. Enable only the search and integration tools you intend Row-Bot to use. 3. Confirm external services are healthy before relying on them. 4. Use eager mode temporarily only when testing compatibility with an older model or integration. 5. Review approvals before any action that writes, sends, or changes external state. ## What Is Saved The capability-loading choice and tool settings are local global preferences. Per-task skill activation is stored separately and does not change this tool policy. ## Privacy And Safety Auto mode reduces schemas in the model prompt, but it does not make a networked tool local. When Row-Bot actually calls a hosted model, remote MCP server, plugin service, account integration, or channel, the data required by that operation can leave your machine.
